description: Committee recommends increasing Biosolids Forcemain project budget by $21.6 million.

chips.text: Recommended
Reallocates $15.6M from Bioreactor Expansion, $3.9M from Biogas Energy.
Councillor Dubois questioned guaranteed cost recovery for infrastructure outside city limits.
Martensville residents are served by this infrastructure project.
Committee recommends interim funding for infrastructure outside city limits.
Administration committed to improving accounting processes for funding reallocations.

description: New tiered residential parking permit fees proposed.
Digital visitor permits, mail-out ticketing pilot proposed.
Multi-unit permit eligibility limited in growth areas.

chips.text: Recommended
Proposed tiered permit fees: $25 for first, $30 for second, $40 for third.
Councillor Jefferies stated program's financial basis unchanged since 1999
Residents in RPP zones, especially multi-unit dwellers, affected by permit changes.
Councillor DeBlanc felt pushback on breaking down RPP enforcement costs from city-wide figures.
Tiered permit pricing is a first for resident parking management in Saskatoon.
Number of potential additional multi-unit permits under new rules remains uncalculated.
University Community Association questioned financial accountability, requested RPP forensic audit.
Councillors Parker, McDonald, Timone expressed concerns, not fully supporting recommendations.
Equity concerns raised regarding tiered pricing and multi-unit permit eligibility.
Administration will provide additional program reporting in annual community standards report.

speakers.name: CLinton Ekdahl
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Registered Parking Program and Proposed Alternative Solutions
said: Questioned exclusion of parking ticket revenue from RPP finances.
Requested independent financial forensic audit of RPP since 1998.
Demanded clear, transparent financial records for RPP zones.

description: Leisure center hour reductions saved $240,000 through September.

chips.text: Preliminary savings of $240,000 exceed original $176,000 annual estimate.
Staff projected savings may return to original $176,000 annual estimate.
Residents faced challenges accessing facilities before work or school.
Approximately 50-60 customer feedback submissions opposed reduced hours.
